correctness.rationale: A BV function equals a constant plus a superposition of left steps against −Df. Taking the spacetime Hilbert norm gives an attained one-step maximum (the step profile is continuous, zero at the endpoints, and positive inside). Equality forces the step residuals with the signs of their measure densities to align on one ray almost everywhere. A nontrivial proportionality for distinct knots would persist at a positive time and make a nontrivial combination of distinct steps constant, since the Neumann nullspace of I−P_t is exactly the constants. This gives the complete equality case. Cosine coefficients and integration of (1−exp(−π²n²t))² reproduce the displayed J_T. Independently derive the image formula by writing the fixed-time derivative as q−2Q_t q+Q_{2t}q, with q(s)=1−2s on (0,1) periodically extended and Q_t the periodic heat semigroup of diffusivity 1/4 (the sine multipliers are exp(−π²n²t)). Convolving the sawtooth derivative q′=−2+2Σδ_k gives Q_t q=q−Σ sign(s−k)erfc(|s−k|/√t), yielding (49). On 0<s≤1/2 the nonzero images and their first s-derivatives are O(exp(−c/t)), absorbing powers of t into a slightly smaller exponent. Thus integrating time and then space gives uniform rescaled profile convergence and C² convergence near the candidate knot. A(z)=∫₀¹erfc(z/√u)du is the twice integrated positive erfc tail with A″=4erfc. The increasing erfc hazard (reciprocal ∫₀∞ exp(−v²−2zv)dv) and the log-concave tail-ratio argument give increasing positive hazard for A; therefore A(z)/A(z/√2) decreases strictly from 1 to 0, the latter also by integrating its positive hazard over [z/√2,z]. The unique critical point of G is nondegenerate, and G(∞)=2(2−√2)/(3√π) is strictly lower; the uniform profile gap localizes every maximizing knot and the C² limit proves uniqueness on each half for small T. The absolutely convergent second derivative of the spectral correction gives J_T″<−2T+1, proving the midpoint result including T=1/2. Independent numerical replay using the erf power series and I(z)=(z+2z³/3)erfc(z)+2[1−(1+z²)exp(−z²)]/(3√π), an antiderivative of A starting at zero, gives ζ≈0.772397284434471, G(ζ)≈0.257188139594510 and the stated 16.72874596% gain. The frozen checker was inspected but not run. The proof does not classify intermediate horizons or optimize the sufficient 1/2 guarantee.

value.rationale: Cumulative error on one fixed input is a natural stability benchmark for diffusion. It gives a different sharp Gaussian location than one-time error, an exact correction above the bulk value, complete equality conditions, and a provably different midpoint regime at long horizons. The result is not just an integral of instantaneous optimal values or a numerical maximization at one time.
